name: Standard CO2 Propulsion Cartridge SPC-12
description:
The SPC-12 is a standard 12-gram compressed CO2 cartridge used as a propellant source for pneumatic weapon platforms across multiple manufacturers. The cartridge is a simple, unregulated consumable — a small steel cylinder containing liquid CO2 under pressure, with a pierceable brass seal that the weapon's action punctures to release gas into the firing chamber.

The SPC-12 is not proprietary to any weapons manufacturer and is produced by dozens of industrial suppliers for applications ranging from beverage carbonation to fire suppression. Its widespread availability and low cost make it the default propellant for weapons designed to operate outside conventional ammunition supply chains — platforms like the NDP-4 'Stutter' and PSP-2 'Gravel' that prioritize concealability and supply chain anonymity over raw performance.

Each 12g cartridge provides approximately 18 pneumatic discharges at standard pressure, though this varies by weapon platform and ambient temperature. Cold environments reduce cartridge pressure and per-shot velocity, while hot environments increase both — a variable that experienced operators account for but that novice users frequently overlook. The cartridge's steel housing makes it the only component of many pneumatic weapon systems that triggers metal detectors, leading to a black market in polymer-bodied CO2 cartridges that sacrifice some pressure containment for complete scanner invisibility.
legality: Unrestricted — industrial commodity, no weapons classification
specifications:
weight_per_cartridge: 45g (full)
gas_capacity: 12g liquid CO2
shots_per_cartridge: 14-22 depending on platform and temperature
operating_temperature: -5C to 50C (performance varies)
shelf_life: Indefinite if seal intact
storage: No special requirements
variants: SPC-12 Polymer (scanner-invisible housing, 10g capacity, reduced pressure)
SPC-12 Extended (16g capacity, oversized housing, incompatible with some compact platforms)
SPC-12 Nitrogen (N2 fill instead of CO2, marginally different ballistics, used in cold-weather operations)
cultural_context: The SPC-12 is invisible in the most literal sense — it is an industrial commodity that does not register as weapons-related in any procurement database, shipping manifest, or retail transaction. An operator can buy a case of SPC-12 cartridges at any hardware store, and no one will wonder why. This anonymity is the foundation of the pneumatic weapons ecosystem in GLMZ: the weapons are exotic, but the propellant is mundane. Street operators sometimes carry SPC-12 cartridges as their only visible equipment, knowing that the cartridges alone prove nothing and that the weapon they power can be concealed or disposed of independently.
story_hooks: A shipping anomaly has flagged an unusually large order of SPC-12 cartridges to a residential address — hundreds of cartridges, enough for thousands of pneumatic weapon discharges, and the buyer has no industrial or commercial reason for the purchase.

A polymer-bodied SPC-12 variant has been linked to three scanner-bypass incidents at corporate facilities — the manufacturer is untraceable, and the cartridge design includes engineering refinements that suggest the creator has access to pressure vessel manufacturing expertise.
